mappings.rationale: The organization must hold documented continuity plans that are workable, assign roles, and be reviewed and updated regularly; BCD-01.7 requires process owners to maintain formal BC/DR plans detailed and accurate enough to sustain or restore operations, and BCD-06 supplies the ongoing update of those plans as people, processes and technology change.

The clause demands an incident response structure with activation thresholds, a coordinated response and internal/external communications; BCD-01.5 defines the criteria that must be met to initiate continuity plans, IRO-07 is the integrated cross-functional response team that operates and coordinates the response, and BCD-01.6 carries the internal and external status communications.

Warning and communication requires the means of communication to remain available during a disruption and structured communication with responders and authorities; BCD-10.4 maintains command-and-control over alternate communication channels with alternative decision makers, and BCD-01.6 delivers the structured status communication to internal and external stakeholders — the detection and incident-record limbs are covered by monitoring and incident controls not credited here.

Each plan must state purpose, activation criteria, roles, resources and interdependencies and collectively recover prioritized activities within their RTO; BCD-01.7 requires the plan content to be detailed, accurate and representative of current operations, and BCD-01.4 binds recovery operations to defined RTOs and RPOs.

The clause obliges documented procedures to transition from response back to normal operations and to verify systems and data are restored; BCD-12 is the secure recovery and reconstitution of assets to a known state after a disruption, and BCD-02.1 covers resuming all missions and business functions within the plan's recovery objectives.

The exercise programme must validate the continuity arrangements over time at planned intervals and after significant change; BCD-04 is precisely the mechanism for conducting tests and exercises that evaluate the contingency plan's effectiveness and the organisation's readiness to execute it.

The programme must include varied exercise types from tabletop to live rehearsal, including technology recovery tests and exercises involving external parties; BCD-04 supplies the exercise mechanism, BCD-04.1 covers coordination with internal and external parties responsible for related plans, and BCD-04.2 covers the technology-focused testing at alternate storage and processing sites.

The organization must decide what to monitor and measure, how and when, and evaluate BCMS performance with retained evidence; GOV-05 is the mechanism for developing, reporting and monitoring programme measures of performance and GOV-05.1 supplies the KPIs and trend analysis — SCF frames this at security-programme level rather than BCMS level, hence medium.

BC procedures must be evaluated at planned intervals and after exercises, incidents and significant change, testing whether RTO/RPO can actually be met; BCD-04 provides the effectiveness evaluation through testing and BCD-06 forces plans to be revisited when people, process or technology change — the BIA-conformance limb sits in RSK-08 and is not credited here.

After each exercise the organization must capture lessons learned, report findings and track corrective actions to completion; BCD-05 is SCF's root cause analysis and lessons-learned mechanism for contingency plans and BCD-06 drives the resulting plan updates — SCF anchors BCD-05 to plan activation rather than to exercises, so the fit is clear but partial.
